Tell me in about 200 words why people in India are switching to UPI, with a short list of 3 reasons
9:19 PM

People in India are switching to UPI because it makes paying as easy as scanning a code, and it costs most people nothing. A chai seller, a big mall and a friend splitting dinner can all take the same payment in seconds, so it works almost everywhere you go.

The three main reasons:

Speed and ease: Scan a QR code or type a phone number, enter your PIN, and you're done. There's no cash to count, no change to wait for and no card to swipe.
No cost to you: Sending money to people and paying most shops carries no fee, unlike cards or wallets that often add charges.
One system for every bank: You link your bank account to PhonePe, Google Pay, Paytm or your bank's own app. Money moves straight from account to account, day or night, even on holidays.

Cheap smartphones and mobile data helped a lot. Small shops don't need a card machine either, just a printed QR code. Every payment also leaves a record on your phone, so keeping track of spending is easier than with cash.

Plan a 3 day trip to Jaipur for my parents
9:22 PM

Here's a relaxed 3 day Jaipur plan for your parents, with a slow morning start, a long afternoon rest and no more than two big sights a day.

Day 1, the old city: City Palace and Jantar Mantar in the morning, then lunch and a rest. In the evening, a photo stop at Hawa Mahal and a slow walk through Johari Bazaar.
Day 2, forts: Amber Fort early, before the heat and crowds. A jeep ride up saves them the steep climb. Stop at Jal Mahal on the way back, rest after lunch, and watch the sunset from Nahargarh Fort.
Day 3, easy day: Albert Hall Museum and Birla Mandir in the morning, then shopping for block prints, jewellery and blue pottery. End with dinner and folk music at Chokhi Dhani.

Oct to Mar is the best time to go, so the weather will be kind. Stay near MI Road or the old city so every sight is a short ride away.
